findings.issue: Both claim statistical resolution the project's own paired tables refute. Intro: "Sven reaches a lower final validation loss than Adam, AdamW, SGD, SGD with momentum and RMSprop on all four of our perceptron tasks, with paired per-seed margins clearing a 95% confidence interval." Conclusion: "...lower final loss than every first-order and Kronecker-factored baseline we ran, by margins that clear a 95% paired interval." Per analysis/tables/paired_val_*: on MNIST label regression Adam [-0.01249, +0.002162], AdamW [-0.01093, +0.001801], SGD [-0.005567, +0.001629] and SGD+momentum [-0.00433, +0.000391] all cover zero (`significant False`); on toy_1d SGD [-0.003271, +0.001103] and RMSprop [-0.000639, +9.1e-05] cover zero; on MNIST CE SGD covers zero. Only the polynomial scan supports the sentence. This is also mis-stated in the integrator's own CHANGES_v2.md line 156 ("Sven beats Adam and AdamW significantly" on MNIST — true for CE, false for label regression). §4.1 already prints the honest counts (11 of 13 worse, only 4 resolvably), so the paper contradicts itself.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the significance clause from both sentences and keep the seed-mean claim, or scope it: "...on all four perceptron tasks; the margin clears a 95% paired interval on the polynomial scan and on cross-entropy, and is within seed noise against Adam, AdamW and SGD on MNIST label regression (Appendix F)." Generate the count of resolved wins as a macro rather than asserting it in prose.

findings.issue: "...\numNanogptSvenRank{} of \numNanogptNMethods{} behind AdamW, and those leads are resolved by the same paired test." AdamW's nanoGPT lead is paired difference +0.00218 with interval [-0.0226, 0.0269] — it covers zero, and the *same paragraph two sentences earlier* calls it "a tie, which we report as one." The sentence therefore asserts the opposite of what it just said, and of Table paired_val_exp_nanogpt_speedrun (significant False).
findings.suggested_fix: Exclude nanoGPT from the clause: "...and HIG's and MuonW's leads are resolved by the same paired test; AdamW's is not — that ordering is the tie above."

findings.issue: "HIG leads both synthetic regressions and MuonW both MNIST and both CIFAR-10 scans, by margins a paired test resolves" (and App. F: "HIG's [advantage] on both synthetics"). On toy_1d HIG's paired difference is +5.07e-07 with interval [-3.17e-07, 1.33e-06] — `significant False`, 0 of 15 pairs either way. Only the polynomial lead is resolved. (MuonW's four leads do check out: MNIST LR/CE and CIFAR LR/CE are all `significant True`.) App. E is careful about exactly this scan ("no ranking on that scan should be read as resolved"), so these two sentences contradict it.
findings.suggested_fix: "HIG leads the polynomial regression resolvably and the 1D scan within seed noise, and MuonW leads both MNIST and both CIFAR-10 scans resolvably." Fix the App. F sentence the same way.

findings.issue: Four classes of edit are in black, violating the binding markup rule ("every inserted or changed span must be inside \new{} or newtext; changed captions are blue; unchanged text stays byte-identical"). (a) :166 Algorithm 1's caption was rewritten — "considers only the $k$ largest singular values, and sets singular values that are a factor of rtol smaller than the largest singular value to zero" became "keeps the $k$ largest singular values and zeroes those a factor rtol below the largest" — in black; only the appended Gram sentence is blue. (b) :343 two Related-Work sentences were rewritten in black: Shampoo/SOAP ("...preconditioning matrices, accumulating second moment statistics over time rather than computing a per-step spectral decomposition as Sven does" → "...preconditioners accumulated over time, rather than a per-step spectral decomposition") and Levenberg–Marquardt ("interpolates between gradient descent and Gauss-Newton via a damping parameter, shrinking all singular values uniformly; Sven's hard truncation of the top-$k$ directions provides an alternative regularization strategy at significantly lower wall-time cost" → "shrinks all singular values uniformly via a damping parameter; Sven's hard truncation is an alternative regularization strategy"). The second silently drops an unsupported wall-time claim — exactly the case the contract says must be marked. (c) :421 Conclusion paragraph 2 rewritten in black: "(weight decay, ... among them)" → em-dashes, "adds to this toolkit a principled mechanism" → "adds a principled mechanism", "can be composed with these existing techniques" → "composes with them". (d) App. C subsections renamed or added in black and rendering black in the PDF (p17–p21): "Datasets"→"Datasets and Splits", "Model Architecture"→"Model Architectures", "Hyperparameter Scans"→"Hyperparameter Grids", plus two entirely new subsections "Evaluation Protocol" and "Compute and Wall-Time Measurement". Verified by word-diffing the two .tex files with \new{}/newtext spans elided.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap each changed span in \new{}: the two rewritten sentences of Algorithm 1's caption; the two Related-Work sentences at :343; the rewritten clauses at :421; and every renamed or new (sub)section title in app_exp_details.tex (\subsection{\new{Datasets and Splits}} etc.). Re-run the elided word-diff as a gate — it should come back empty apart from deletions.

findings.location: iclr_manuscript/iclr2026_conference_v2.tex:692 (Appendix N, "Decreasing Memory Requirements", opening sentences — black, unchanged)
findings.issue: "While the computational cost in the over-parametrized limit is only a factor of $k$ higher than SGD, the memory requirements can be significantly higher... computing the Jacobian requires storing a number of model copies equal to the batch size." Both halves are exactly the claims the revision retracted: §2.3 replaced the identical sentence with a `% OLD:` note saying "The claim changed materially: the implementation used for every experiment in this paper has a cost that is independent of $k$", and App. D states the Jacobian is never materialised (verified against sven/sven/nn/gram_wrapper.py, which builds $G=JJ^\top$ from one forward + one backward and never forms the $(B,P)$ Jacobian under the default `hooks` capture). A reader who reaches App. N is told the opposite of the paper's central efficiency claim, in black type so it reads as unrevised fact.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the paragraph with a blue one, e.g. \new{The Gram implementation of Appendix~\ref{app:gram} removes the $k$ dependence of the solve and never stores $M$; what remains is the cost of capturing the per-sample gradients. The two knobs below were proposed against the older explicit-Jacobian cost model, and Appendix~\ref{app:gram_knobs} restates them in the Gram representation.} Keep the removed sentences as a `% OLD:` comment.

findings.issue: "We train small three-layer MLPs for each task" now directly follows the blue paragraph that names nanoGPT — an 826,368-parameter decoder-only transformer — as one of the three headline tasks, and precedes a protocol paragraph that says "20 for the perceptrons and 50 for nanoGPT". The sentence is false as it now stands, and because it is black a reader takes it as the unrevised description of the whole experimental setup. App. C.2 (blue) has the correct statement ("MLPs ... for the regression and MNIST experiments").
findings.suggested_fix: \new{We train small three-layer MLPs on the four perceptron tasks and a four-layer decoder-only transformer on nanoGPT, using identical initialization and data loading order across all optimizers to ensure fair comparison.}

findings.location: iclr_manuscript/iclr2026_conference_v2.tex:212 (§2.1 dimension box) vs :480, :527, :528, :586, :611 (Appendices A and B) and :738-777 (Appendix Q algorithms)
findings.issue: The rename $|D|\to B$, $N\to P$ was applied to the main text and the new appendices but not to Appendices A and B, which remain byte-identical and use $N$ for the *parameter count*. §2.1's blue box explicitly instructs the reader to "keep them apart: ... $P > N$, a statement about the dataset", so App. B's unchanged sentence "If the batch size $|B|$ is greater or equal than the number of parameters $N$ then $\gamma$ is generically invertible... when $|B|<N$, the metric $\gamma$ is definitely singular" is, under the paper's own stated notation, a false statement about the training-set size. findings.suggested_fix: Rename in Appendices A and B with blue \new{} marks ($N\to P$ for parameters; $B\to\mathcal{B}$ or $|\mathcal{B}|\to B$ for the batch), and add one blue sentence at the top of Appendix Q noting that the $B$ of Algorithms 3–4 is the projected matrix, not the batch size. findings.location: iclr_manuscript/sections_v2/app_gram.tex:197-200 (eqn:gram_rank) and app_spectra.tex:199-202 (eqn:rank_law); restated at v2:403, app_exp_details.tex:215, app_lims_results.tex, app_batchsize.tex:134, app_cifar.tex:15, v2:419
findings.issue: The same identity is given twice as a numbered equation with two labels and two different strictness conventions — eqn:gram_rank uses $\sigma_i > \texttt{rtol}\cdot\sigma_1$, eqn:rank_law uses $\sigma_i \ge \texttt{rtol}\cdot\sigma_1$ — while sven/sven/opt/sven.py:464 implements `keep = sigma > self.rtol * sigma[0]` (strict). The two appendices also disagree on the order the cuts are applied: App. D.4 says "the $k$ largest are kept, and of those the ones with $\sigma_i \le \texttt{rtol}\cdot\sigma_1$ are dropped" (which is what the code does) while App. O:198 says "rtol is applied first and $k$ second". Both orders give the same min(), but the paper states an identity it verifies on 49,040 steps, so the boundary convention and the order should be one thing. The identity itself is then restated in prose seven more times.

findings.issue:
"...the hooks capture's step time grows with parameter count with a fitted exponent of 
umProfMnistWidthHooksStepExp{} and its peak memory with 
umProfMnistWidthHooksMemExp{}, against 
umProfMnistWidthFullStepExp{} and 
umProfMnistWidthFullMemExp{} for the dense capture: the former tracks the baselines, the latter tracks the Jacobian." The values are 0 and 0.49 against 0.15 and 0.97. findings.location: Throughout the new text: v2:394,396,403,427; app_cifar.tex:6; app_transformers.tex:123,133; app_spectra.tex:207,221; app_budget.tex:11; app_robustness.tex:165,171; app_fig5.tex:86; app_profiling.tex:20; app_gram.tex:398
findings.issue: A meta-honesty register recurs at least twelve times — "a tie, which we report as one", "we report it as one rather than as a win", "and we state it here rather than only in an appendix", "the appendix says so at the outset", "we say so rather than reporting the rank table alone", "The honest summary is...", "This is the truncation figure we consider honest", "That is a measurement and not a rhetorical point", "Nothing here is excluded from any table elsewhere", "and we count it as one", "we do not claim that it does" (×3), "stated because it moves numbers and not as a tuning tip". Individually each is fine; together they read as protesting honesty rather than reporting, which is its own kind of marketing, and they occupy space in a paper that had to move Table 1 out of §4 for room. The style brief asks for concise prose matching the existing voice, which states results flatly.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep at most three (the nanoGPT tie, the equal-budget summary, the minimum-norm non-result) and delete the rest — the numbers and the fin./att. columns already carry the honesty. Reclaimed space goes to §4's missing table.

findings.issue: Appendix M opens by restating the loss in the superseded unsigned form, $L(\theta)=\sum_\alpha((\ell^\alpha)^{\kappa/2})^{2/\kappa}$ with $\mathcal{R}_{\rm eff}=\ell^{\kappa/2}$, in unchanged black type — but §2.1's Eq. 8 was rewritten (blue) to expose $\mathcal{R}_{\rm eff}$ as the defined object, and §2.1 then adopts the *signed* row definition $\mathcal{R}_{\rm eff}=\mathrm{sign}(r)|r|^{\kappa}$ that the appendix itself credits with making $\kappa=1$ runnable. The appendix therefore introduces its own subject with the form the revision replaced, one paragraph before explaining why that form was the problem.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the black preamble with \eqref{eqn:kappa_generalization} plus one blue sentence recalling the signed row definition, so the appendix starts from the notation §2.1 now establishes.

findings.issue: "In the untruncated solve, changing $\kappa$ rescales every row of $M$ by the same factor on a scalar-residual problem, and the pseudoinverse undoes it exactly." It is not a common factor: with $\mathcal{R}_{\rm eff}=\mathrm{sign}(r)|r|^\kappa$ the row is $\kappa|r_\alpha|^{\kappa-1}\partial r_\alpha/\partial\theta$, i.e. a per-row diagonal rescaling $D=\kappa\,\mathrm{diag}(|r_\alpha|^{\kappa-1})$. The stated conclusion is nevertheless exactly right — $(DM)^+(D\mathcal{R}_1)=M^+\mathcal{R}_1$ for full-row-rank $M$, giving $\text{update}_\kappa=(2/\kappa)\,\text{update}_2$ — so only the mechanism sentence is wrong.
findings.suggested_fix: "...rescales the rows of $M$ by a diagonal factor that the pseudoinverse cancels exactly (for full row rank), leaving the $\kappa$ update equal to $2/\kappa$ times the $\kappa=2$ update."

findings.issue:

umPolyNPairedMethods, the baselines, is 14), so the abstract claims one opponent too many; §4's "The field is

umNanogptSvenMemVsAdamW{}$	imes$ Adam's on the transformer" (:111, :328) and "
umSvenStepVsAdamMin--
umSvenStepVsAdamMax$	imes$ Adam's step" (:396, :419, :427) — but Adam was not run on either language-model scan (App. C: AdamW, Muon, MuonW, SOAP), and the macro is the ratio to AdamW.
findings.suggested_fix: "...against a field of fourteen baselines" (or "a field of fifteen optimizers including Sven"), and list Sven in the §4 enumeration. Write "Adam's on the perceptrons and AdamW's on the transformer", or rename the macro to make the denominator explicit.

findings.issue: The clean 4-pass build was obtained with TEXINPUTS pointed at local shims, because this machine's TeX Live 2018 has no algpseudocode, algorithmicx, bbm or nicefrac (kpsewhich: MISSING). The contract requires the file to compile from inside iclr_manuscript/ with the stock toolchain, which cannot be checked here (nor could the original).

summary:
Adversarial review of iclr_manuscript/iclr2026_conference_v2.tex (read-only; nothing edited). What holds up: the build is genuinely clean — 4 passes, 0 errors, 0 undefined references or citations, 0 overfull boxes >10 pt, 92 pages with sec:code on p9 so the 9-page main-text limit is met; all 477 \num… macros used are defined among the 1,249 generated; all 45 \includegraphics targets and all tables_v2 inputs exist; no real duplicate labels and no unresolved \ref; appendix lettering is A–R exactly as planned; newtext is balanced with no float inside it; the rendered PDF is anonymity-clean. I verified the Gram derivation against sven/sven/nn/gram_wrapper.py and sven/sven/opt/sven.py (the M^+R = M^T[sum u_i σ_i^-2 u_i^T R] identity, float64 Gram accumulation, the min(k, rtol-rank) truncation and the signed-residual row definition all check out) and the datasets, splits, model sizes, epochs and every hyperparameter grid against EXPERIMENTS.md and experiments/configs (all match, including use_gram: true on the MLP scans, so "all experiments use the Gram implementation" is supported).

The problems cluster in three places. (1) Claim discipline: three separate sentences assert 95% paired resolution that the project's own analysis/tables/paired_val_* files refute — the Intro and Conclusion claim resolved margins over Adam/AdamW/SGD/SGD+momentum/RMSprop that cover zero on MNIST label regression and on 1D; §4.1 says AdamW's nanoGPT lead "is resolved" two sentences after calling it a tie; and the Limitations plus App. F claim HIG's lead is resolved on "both synthetics" when the 1D interval covers zero. (2) Markup: four classes of edit are in black — Algorithm 1's caption, two rewritten Related-Work sentences (one of which silently drops an unsupported wall-time claim), Conclusion paragraph 2, and five renamed or new App. C subsection headings — found by word-diffing the two files with the blue spans elided. (3) Stale black text that the revision contradicts: App. N still opens with "only a factor of k higher than SGD" and "storing a number of model copies equal to the batch size" — exactly what §2.3 retracted with a % OLD: note — and §4 still says "We train small three-layer MLPs for each task" one paragraph after introducing nanoGPT. Two further high items: the fig:cost_memory caption claims a 163M-parameter point the figure does not contain (its x axis stops at ResNet18), and the N→P rename was not carried into Appendices A and B, where N still means the parameter count, so App. B's "|B| < N ⇒ singular" is false under §2.1's own new notation — which undoes the single most important promised clarification (R3's dimensionality misread).

Verdict: needs fixes before submission. The eight high findings are all local edits; the mediums worth doing are the App. O self-contradiction on the kept-energy mechanism, §4's single-float layout (Table 1 on p32, the spectra figure on p58, the cost figure on p83), Fig. 1's unreadable MNIST panel and shared 9-entry legend, ~20 uncited floats plus an entirely uncited Appendix H, the grid tables landing inside subsection C.5, and the seven hand-typed campaign totals that `python -m paper_assets` does not regenerate (a stale-number trap on the next refresh).
